properties.name: Mount Whaleback (Newman)

capacity.n: nominal ore capacity, as stated by Wikipedia

properties.note: Feeds Newman Hub to Port Hedland. BHP's Western Australia Iron Ore produced 291.2 Mt in FY2025-26 on a 100% basis (BHP operational review, 16 July 2026).

properties.name: Jimblebar

output.n: saleable iron ore, FY2025-26, 100% basis (BHP holds 85%)

properties.note: BHP Pilbara mine east of Newman, railed to Port Hedland. The figure is on a 100% basis; BHP holds 85% of Western Australia Iron Ore.

properties.name: South Flank / Mining Area C

output.n: saleable iron ore, Area C joint venture incl. South Flank, FY2025-26, 100% basis computed from BHP's 85% share

properties.note: South Flank is BHP's largest Pilbara mine; Argus Media gives it an 80 Mt/y nameplate, and BHP reports it exceeded nameplate in FY2025-26.

properties.name: Yandicoogina (Yandi)

capacity.n: annual production capacity, as stated by Wikipedia

properties.note: Rio Tinto Pilbara mine. Rio Tinto's Pilbara iron ore production was 245.7 Mt in the first nine months of 2026 (100% basis, Rio Tinto, 14 October 2026).

properties.name: Paraburdoo
properties.note: Rio Tinto Pilbara hub (Channar, Eastern Range, Paraburdoo and Western Range, opened 2024). The point is the town; the mine site is nearby.

properties.name: Iron Bridge (Fortescue)
properties.note: Magnetite project about 145 km south of Port Hedland. Fortescue holds 69%; FY2026-27 guidance is 11-14 Mt on a 100% basis (Fortescue, 31 July 2026).

properties.name: Roy Hill
properties.operator: Hancock Prospecting 70%, Marubeni 15%, POSCO 12.5%, China Steel 2.5%

capacity.n: nameplate per the Wikipedia infobox; the article text says 55 Mt/y

properties.note: Independent Pilbara producer with its own rail and Port Hedland berths.

properties.name: Carajás Serra Norte / Serra Leste

output.n: iron ore, Serra Norte and Serra Leste

properties.note: Ships via the EFC railway to Ponta da Madeira. Vale group iron ore production was 336 Mt in 2025 (Vale, 4Q25 results).

properties.name: S11D (Carajás)
properties.note: Vale reports a record 86.0 Mt in 2025 (4Q25 results).

properties.name: Simandou (Blocks 1-4)
properties.operator: Rio Tinto / Winning Consortium (SMB-Winning) / Baowu / Guinea state

capacity.n: combined SimFer and WCS export capacity after commissioning and ramp-up (a target, not yet reached)

properties.statusNote: Operations started 11 November 2025; ramp-up continues, with an annualised run-rate of about 10 Mtpa in Q3 2026 (Rio Tinto, 14 October 2026).
properties.note: Rio Tinto and its partners marked the start of operations on 11 November 2025, with commissioning under way. Rio Tinto targets a 60 Mtpa run-rate for SimFer in H2 2028. The point is the centre of the range.

properties.name: Kiruna
properties.note: World's largest underground iron ore mine; ore exported via Narvik (Norway) and Luleå.

properties.name: Malmberget
properties.note: LKAB's second Norrbotten mine; pellets/fines via Luleå.

properties.name: Sishen
properties.note: Feeds Saldanha Bay via the 861 km Sishen-Saldanha line.

properties.name: Iron Ore Company of Canada (Labrador City)
properties.operator: Iron Ore Company of Canada (Rio Tinto 58.7%, Mitsubishi 26.2%, LIORC 15.1%)

capacity.n: nominal mining capacity (ore mined; saleable output is lower)

properties.note: Concentrate and pellets shipped via Sept-Iles.

properties.name: North Antelope Rochelle

output.n: coal, converted from short tons at 0.9072 (Peabody states its volumes in short tons, Q1 2026 results release)

properties.note: Largest US coal mine; Powder River Basin (Wyoming), low-sulphur thermal coal.

properties.name: Black Thunder
properties.note: Powder River Basin output fell below 200 Mt in 2024 (185.15 Mt for Wyoming, Cowboy State Daily).

properties.name: Bulianta (Shendong)
properties.note: Underground longwall mine in Ordos, Inner Mongolia. Output is a GlobalData estimate.

properties.name: Haerwusu (Shendong)
properties.note: Large open-pit mine in Ordos, Inner Mongolia. Output is a GlobalData estimate.

properties.name: Adaro / Tutupan (Tabalong)
properties.operator: Adaro Indonesia (AlamTri Resources, formerly Adaro Energy)

capacity.n: coal, roughly 110 kt a day; as stated by Wikipedia

properties.note: South Kalimantan (Tabalong), shipped by river barge to the Taboneo transhipment point.

properties.name: Cerrejon
properties.statusNote: Output cut to 16.8 Mt in 2025 after production cuts announced in March 2025 (Glencore).
properties.note: Colombia's largest coal mine, railed to Puerto Bolívar. Wikipedia gives 32.7 Mt for 2016.

properties.name: Goonyella Riverside

output.n: Goonyella saleable coal, FY2025-26, 100% basis computed from BHP's 50% share

properties.note: BMA mine in the Bowen Basin, shipped via Hay Point and Dalrymple Bay. BMA produced 18.6 Mt in FY2025-26 on a BHP-share basis (37.3 Mt at 100%).

properties.name: Peak Downs

output.n: Peak Downs saleable coal, FY2025-26, 100% basis computed from BHP's 50% share

properties.note: BMA open-cut metallurgical coal mine, Bowen Basin.

properties.name: Saraji

capacity.n: saleable coal; the source says capability can exceed this (BHP compliance report)

output.n: Saraji saleable coal, FY2025-26, 100% basis computed from BHP's 50% share

properties.note: BMA mine in the Bowen Basin. Output fell 3% in FY2025-26.

properties.name: Elga (Elga-1/2)
properties.operator: Elgaugol (A-Property, which bought Mechel's 51% stake in April 2020)
properties.note: Eastern Siberia (Yakutia) coking coal. Mechel closed the sale of the Elga coal complex to A-Property on 22 April 2020 (Interfax). Wikipedia gives the Ulak-Elga railway 30 Mt/y by 2023 and a mine capacity of 9 Mt/y, which is not shown because it is hard to reconcile with the railway.

properties.name: Grootegeluk

capacity.n: final coal products, as stated by Wikipedia

properties.note: Supplies Eskom's Matimba/Medupi plus export via Richards Bay.

properties.name: Tavan Tolgoi
properties.operator: Erdenes Mongol / Mongolian Mining Corp (Ukhaa Khudag)
properties.note: Mongolian coking coal trucked and railed to China (Gashuunsukhait/Ceke).

properties.name: Escondida
properties.note: World's largest copper mine. Mining.com's 2025 ranking gives 1,347.6 kt of copper for calendar 2025.

properties.name: Collahuasi

output.n: copper, 100% basis; Glencore reports 177.7 kt for its 44% share

properties.note: Chile, Tarapacá region. Glencore reports 177.7 kt of copper in concentrate for its 44% share in 2025.

properties.name: Grasberg
properties.statusNote: Running below normal after the 2025 Block Cave landslide: output fell to about 30% of normal at one point, concentrate supply to the Gresik smelter resumed in August 2026, and full capacity is expected by early 2028 (Mining.com; Katadata, September 2026; Kontan, 18 September 2026).
properties.note: Concentrate supply to the new Freeport smelter in Gresik resumed in August 2026 (Kontan, 18 September 2026).

properties.name: Kamoa-Kakula
properties.note: 2025 output was within guidance after a flooding stoppage (Ivanhoe, reported by Reuters, 15 January 2026). The on-site smelter started up at the end of 2025.

properties.name: Cerro Verde
properties.operator: Freeport-McMoRan 53.5% / Sumitomo Metal Mining 21% / Buenaventura (as stated for 2015)
properties.note: About 20 miles southwest of Arequipa. Wikipedia gives a designed output of about 1.0 billion lb of copper and 23 million lb of molybdenum a year after the 2015 expansion.

properties.name: Antamina

output.n: copper in concentrate, 100% basis computed from Glencore's 33.75% share (Glencore 2025 production report); the Mining.com ranking gives 368 kt

properties.note: About 15% of Peruvian copper output; slurry pipeline to Huarmey port. Zinc is the main by-product.

properties.name: El Teniente
properties.note: World's largest underground copper mine.

properties.name: Chuquicamata
properties.note: Now underground; includes Codelco's Chuquicamata smelter and refinery.

properties.name: Los Pelambres
properties.note: Also 46,600 oz of gold in 2024 (Wikipedia); concentrate pipeline to Los Vilos.

properties.name: Quellaveco
properties.note: Anglo American majority, Mitsubishi minority.

properties.name: Tenke Fungurume

capacity.n: copper cathode; CMOC says capacity exceeds 450 kt/y with five production lines (CMOC 2025 ESG report)

output.n: copper, about 519 kt per Mining.com ranking

properties.note: Produces copper cathode and cobalt hydroxide; DRC cobalt exports drive the cobalt price. CMOC holds 80% (CMOC 2025 ESG report).

properties.name: Kansanshi

capacity.n: ore processing capacity after the S3 expansion

properties.note: The S3 expansion reached commercial production on 1 December 2025 (Wikipedia).

properties.name: Oyu Tolgoi
properties.operator: Oyu Tolgoi LLC (Rio Tinto 66%, Erdenes Oyu Tolgoi 34%)

capacity.n: copper expected at full production (a target); the source also quotes 430 kt

properties.note: All concentrate is trucked to China (Gashuunsukhait/Ganqimaodu). Rio Tinto reports the mine running at an annualised rate of about 450 kt of copper in Q3 2026 (14 October 2026).

properties.name: Cobre Panama
properties.statusNote: Ordered shut in late 2023; stockpile processing has been running since May 2026 while talks with the government continue (Mining.com, 29 July 2026).
properties.note: First Quantum commissioned the first of three milling circuits in May 2026 and produced its first copper concentrate from stockpiled ore in Q2 2026 (Mining.com, 29 July 2026).

properties.name: Morenci
properties.note: North America's largest copper mine.

properties.name: Bingham Canyon (Kennecott)
properties.note: Utah open pit with an on-site smelter and refinery. Kennecott finished rebuilding its flash converting furnace at the end of August 2026 (Rio Tinto, 14 October 2026).

properties.name: Norilsk-Talnakh (Nornickel)

output.n: nickel, Nornickel group (not Norilsk mines only); copper 425 kt

properties.note: Nornickel group figures, not mine-only: copper 425 kt in 2025 (Nornickel, 28 January 2026).

properties.name: Greenbushes (Talison)
properties.operator: Talison Lithium (Tianqi Lithium Energy Australia 51%, a venture of Tianqi 51% and IGO 49%; Albemarle 49%)

capacity.n: spodumene concentrate, as stated by Wikipedia (undated)

properties.note: Hard-rock spodumene; IGO holds a 24.99% indirect interest and guides 1.55-1.75 Mt for FY2026-27 on a 100% basis (IGO, 27 August 2026). Production was scaled back in January 2024 on weak EV demand (Wikipedia).

properties.name: Pilgangoora (Pilbara Minerals / PLS)
properties.note: PLS restarted the Ngungaju plant on 1 July 2026 and is studying a P2000 expansion to about 2.0 Mtpa (PLS, 30 July 2026). Expansions to 680 kt/y and 1 Mt/y were planned in 2023 (Mining Technology).

properties.name: Salar de Atacama brines (SQM / Albemarle)
properties.operator: SQM and Albemarle (SQM's operations folded into Codelco-SQM Nova Andino Litio JV, Dec 2025)
properties.note: Brine extraction by SQM and Albemarle.

properties.name: Mutanda
properties.statusNote: Closed in November 2019; Glencore reports the restart of mining operations in 2025.
properties.note: Glencore reports 247.8 kt of copper and 33.5 kt of cobalt for KCC and Mutanda together in 2025 (Glencore, 29 January 2026).

properties.name: Kamoto (KCC)
properties.note: Described as the largest active cobalt mine in the world (2022); also 270 kt of copper in 2020 (Wikipedia). Glencore reports KCC and Mutanda together at 247.8 kt of copper and 33.5 kt of cobalt in 2025.

properties.name: Weipa (East Weipa, Andoom, Amrun)
properties.note: Most ore feeds the Gladstone refineries (QAL, Yarwun); the Amrun first shipment was in December 2018.

properties.name: Muruntau
properties.note: Giant open pit in the Kyzylkum; the source gives no output after 2014.

properties.name: Kibali
properties.operator: Barrick (45%), AngloGold Ashanti (45%), SOKIMO (10%) as of 2020

capacity.n: ore the plant can process, as stated by Wikipedia

properties.name: Pueblo Viejo

output.n: gold, as reported by Barrick; basis not stated by the source (it may be the 60% share)

properties.note: Expansion requiring new tailings dam proposed 2019.

properties.name: Boddington
properties.note: Australia's biggest producing gold mine in 2022 (Wikipedia); 98 Mlb of copper in 2023.

properties.name: Cortez (Nevada Gold Mines)
properties.note: Pipeline and Cortez Hills deposits; about 100 km southwest of Elko, Nevada.

properties.name: Cigar Lake
properties.note: Highest-grade uranium mine. Cameco reports 19.1 Mlb (100% basis) in 2025, 1.1 Mlb above plan (World Nuclear News, 17 February 2026).

properties.name: McArthur River

capacity.n: regulated annual limit, as stated by Wikipedia (undated)

properties.statusNote: Care and maintenance from July 2018; Cameco announced in February 2022 it would reopen the mine; 15.1 Mlb produced in 2025.
properties.note: McArthur River/Key Lake produced 15.1 Mlb (100% basis) in 2025, meeting revised guidance (Cameco, via World Nuclear News, 17 February 2026). Milled at Key Lake.

properties.name: Husab
properties.operator: Swakop Uranium (CGN / China-Africa Development Fund ~90%, Epangelo 10%)

capacity.n: potential annual output, as stated by Wikipedia (undated)

properties.note: Open pit near Swakopmund, south of the Rössing mine; production began in late 2016. The point is from OpenStreetMap; the previous point was about 55 km west of the mine.

properties.name: Olympic Dam
properties.note: Polymetallic mine. BHP reports for FY2025-26: 221.3 kt of copper cathode, 231,025 oz of refined gold, 1,100 koz of refined silver and 3,647 t of payable uranium. Wikipedia puts roughly 70% of revenue in copper, 25% in uranium and 5% in silver and gold.

properties.name: Rocanville
properties.note: Expanded significantly in 2017; one of Nutrien's six Saskatchewan potash mines.

properties.name: Belaruskali (Soligorsk)
properties.note: About 20% of global potash supply as of 2019, mostly exported to China; under US, EU, UK and Canadian sanctions.

properties.name: Uralkali (Berezniki / Solikamsk)
properties.note: Five mines and seven mills across Berezniki and Solikamsk.

properties.name: Khouribga phosphate mines (OCP)
properties.note: Phosphate rock is shipped via Jorf Lasfar. The point is the city.

properties.name: Mamatwan
properties.note: Kalahari manganese field, Northern Cape; Wikipedia cites reserves of 433 Mt at 40% Mn.

properties.name: GEMCO (Groote Eylandt)

capacity.n: manganese ore, as stated by Wikipedia citing MineralPrices.com (retrieved 2025)

properties.note: Groote Eylandt, Northern Territory.

properties.name: Mountain Pass
properties.note: Shenghe Resources holds 8% of MP Materials (Wikipedia). Processing of light rare earths restarted in 2022. MP reports 45,455 t of REO in concentrate in 2024.

properties.name: Bayan Obo
properties.note: The mines north of the town accounted for 45% of global rare-earth output as of 2005 (Wikipedia).

properties.name: Mount Weld
properties.note: Feeds Lynas Kuantan separation plant.

properties.name: Red Dog

output.n: zinc in concentrate; lead in concentrate 107 kt

properties.note: Zinc and lead mine in Alaska, operated by Teck on land owned by NANA. Wikipedia gives 515,200 t of zinc, 122,600 t of lead and 283 t of silver for 2008.

properties.name: San Rafael
properties.note: About 12% of world tin in 2014 (Moody's, via Wikipedia); the concentrator was expanding from 2,700 to 2,900 t/day in 2014.

properties.name: Hope Downs

capacity.n: iron ore, stated capacity, as stated by Wikipedia (undated)

properties.note: Five open pits including Hope Downs 4 (2013) and Baby Hope (2018).

properties.name: Mogalakwena
properties.note: Largest open-pit PGM mine. The point is from OpenStreetMap; the previous point was the town of Mokopane.
